critical_code_review_comments: server.py:correct_finding — when there are NO changed fields the code correctly skips overwriting `extracted` and `corrected_fields`, but it still writes `validation_status`/`validation_notes`/`action_required` from `recompute_derived(edits)`. Since edits==prev in the no-change path this is a no-op today, but the code path is fragile: if a future edit ever passes partial fields with the same values, recompute_derived is called with edits (correctly reflecting the current extracted) — currently fine. Consider short-circuiting the whole update when changed==[].

server.py:correct_finding always sets confirmed_at on Correct — spec says confirmed_at is set on Confirm; Correct arguably should use a separate timestamp (e.g. corrected_at). Minor / naming only; behavior matches the review request.

analysis.recompute_derived — validation_status flips to needs_review if any required field is missing and nulls the derived deadlines; this matches Stage 2 behaviour and is exercised by test_correct_recompute_unblocks_deadline.
server.py /accuracy is O(n) over all user findings; fine at Stage 3 scale. If dataset grows, consider aggregation pipeline.
CorrectFindingDialog.jsx uses parseInt with no radix guard but the Input type=number restricts to numerics; acceptable.
